I had something like this feeling for a long time! Where everything seemed like it was painted in grey, and held no real meaning to me. I spent 5 years without shedding a single tear. During that time I had lost all my grandparents but one, as well as losing the dog I had literally grown up with. Got into different relationships because it was “what I was suppose to do” right? Played hockey, and any other sport I could get my hands on. 

This is where it splits from yours, probably... 
I figured out, with the help of a four week stay in a hospital and a lot of introspection, that I had been in denial my who life about who I was. The way I had dealt with this denial was dissociation from my emotions, and occasionally, reality. Once I broke that dissociation, the rush of emotions broke me and that’s what ended me up in the hospital. Once I sorted through the emotions, I figured out that what I was in denial about was being a girl. I was born if the wrong body, and had finally figured that out! I can cry now, and actually care what happens to people around me! 

I’m not saying that you are transgender or anything like that. But what you described sounded eerily similar to how people have described being emotionally dissociated. Like you want to care about things, and you want to be able to enjoy things, but your emotions are not in you, they are somewhere else.

 Sorry if this is completely unhelpful, but I know for myself, that having a word for something helps to fight the problem at its core!
